Riverside County: Housing Choice Vouchers covered 18,410 people in reported households in 2025
HUD counted 9,192 reported Housing Choice Voucher households in Riverside County in 2025.
In Riverside County, 18,410 people lived in reported Housing Choice Voucher households in 2025, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
The number of people was down 1,212 from 19,622 in 2024. Those households numbered 9,192.
HUD reported 10,158 Housing Choice Vouchers available in the county, and 89% of them were in use.
HUD classified 69% of those households as headed by a person who is Black, Native American, Asian or Pacific Islander, or Hispanic. Households paid an average of $571 a month toward rent and utilities, up $18 from $553 in 2024, and their average annual household income was $21,293, up $319 from $20,974 in 2024.
The federal Housing Choice Voucher program helps eligible households rent privately owned homes. Participants generally contribute about 30% of their adjusted monthly income toward rent and utilities, while a local housing agency pays a subsidy to the landlord, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. A household may pay more if it chooses a home whose rent exceeds the agency's payment standard.
Families receiving Housing Choice Vouchers had spent an average of 29 months on waiting lists in 2024, according to the . That average covers families who obtained assistance, not applicants still waiting or never served. HUD also estimates that only one in four eligible families receives federal rental assistance.
